# 2 Baruch Chapter 15 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 15:3 — "crown" as eschatological reward

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-world-to-come is-a-crown" | Literal; "crown" as eschatological metaphor |
| LOGOS | "the world to come is a crown" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "the world to come is a crown" | Both PNEUMA and LOGOS agree |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Unanimous. All three agree on "crown." No divergence.

---

## 15:4 — "long-suffering" vs. "endurance" vs. "patience"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-long-suffering of-this-world" | Literal compound — Syriac aru khol/savlanutho |
| LOGOS | "the long-suffering of this world" | Formal, traditional KJV terminology |
| PNEUMA | "the endurance of this world" | "Endurance" is more natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Long-suffering" is the established theological term for patient endurance under extended trial. "Endurance" is acceptable but lacks the temporal dimension of "long-suffering."

---

## 15:6 — "great sorrow shall produce great glory"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "great-sorrow shall-produce-great-glory" | Literal; hyphenated compounds |
| LOGOS | "great sorrow shall produce great glory" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "Great sorrow will produce great glory" | Only tense/mood differs ("will" for "shall") |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Shall produce" carries the prophetic/declarative force of the Syriac future. "Will produce" is more casual. This is the theological climax of the chapter.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 2** (v.3 was unanimous; only vv.4 and 6 had genuine divergences)
